<reason>CON won the live policy comparison: heavy restriction inflicts a certain loss of advertised posts at thin-budget hosts, while PRO’s hoped-for conversion into paid work and a fairer ladder was asserted, not shown. PRO was sharp on wealth filters and stipend incentives if unpaid labor stays legal, but never named a beneficiary who gains if the two-person charity simply stops, and never neutralized remaining private networks or the non-student carve-out problem.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s contradiction that PRO cannot treat the unpaid door as both unused by working-class applicants (so closing it is costless) and as a harmful filter worth closing—then turning PRO’s 34-year-old concession into “demolition with no beneficiary.”</best_rebuttal>
